column1: # What each library's verification needs in memory. `targo trust` gives a verified
# library a ceiling of RAM / 8; a function that needs more is UNKNOWN, so a floor set
# at a larger ceiling is not reproducible on a smaller host (trust_facts.rs: `row_for`,
# `fits`, `memory_refusal`). One row per library and RAM it was measured on:
#   floor ceiling  GiB of the run that set its floors.tsv floor (one per library), or -
#                  (also when that run's log named none, as a seal from trust main's)
#   host RAM       GiB of the machine the need was measured on, or - with no need
#   run ceiling    GiB of the verifier ceiling that run had, or - with no need
#   need           GiB of the verifier's peak (trustc's memory census), or -
#   bound          `=` the run had room, so this is the need; `>` it ran out, so more; -
# A host reads the row of its own RAM, else the nearest below (a lower bound), else
# the nearest above. `ship trust run --update-ratchet` keeps it current; commit it with
